usage: This is the standard and most common way to say 'I love you' across the Levant. It is used romantically with partners, but is equally common to say to children, parents, and close friends. The ending changes based on the gender of the person you are speaking to.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when addressing a female.

variants.label: to a group (North Levant)
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people in Syrian and Lebanese dialects.

variants.label: to a group (South Levant)
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people in Jordanian and Palestinian dialects.

variants.label: stronger affection (to a man)
variants.note: Literally 'I die in you', used to express intense love or infatuation.

responses.english: You are my life (said to a man).
May God keep you for me (said to a man).

examples.english: I love you so much, my soul.
I love you more (said to a woman).
Do you know that I love you?
